sections.heading: C — Right-of-Way—When to Yield
sections.markdown:
## C — Right-of-Way—When to Yield

FACT_ID: sec05-F01 | anchor: A01
Right-of-way laws order safe smooth flow where paths cross, assign legal fault in crashes and pedestrian injuries, bind every person and vehicle including bicyclists, treat the privilege as given rather than taken, demand yielding even when entitled whenever harm threatens, require settling priority before entering, order immediate proceeding once yielded to, and ask eye contact so the other driver truly sees you [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec05-F02 | anchor: A01
Children play in streets for want of parks, chase pets and balls without heed, and wobble through intersections unsignaled, so drivers owe extreme caution with slowing near schools, playgrounds, and homes because striking a child costs dearly in money, grief, and guilt [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec05-F03 | anchor: A01
Blind street-crossers with guide dogs or tapping canes of all white, white with red tip, or chrome own the right-of-way, and drivers must halt at once outside the crosswalk and stop fifteen feet from a blind person in the roadway or at an intersection [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec05-F04 | anchor: A01
Once the funeral lead vehicle enters an intersection the whole procession may follow through regardless of traffic controls, and every procession vehicle burns headlights warning others never to split or block the line [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec05-F05 | anchor: A02
Always yield entering or crossing unsigned highways by stopping for approaching traffic until safe, at stop signs by halting before the crosswalk for pedestrians and intersection traffic until safe, and at yield signs by slowing to a reasonable pace ready to halt until crossing or merging proves safe [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec05-F06 | anchor: A02
Yield to roadway crossers at marked and unmarked crosswalks alike with extra alertness in school zones and busy foot-traffic areas [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec05-F07 | anchor: A02
Left turns yield to every oncoming vehicle with slowing and halting as needed until a gap clears without interference, and entries from private roads, alleys, driveways, or buildings halt before the sidewalk or crosswalk until safe [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec05-F08 | anchor: A02
Siren or flashing-light police cars, fire engines, and ambulances own the yield with drivers pulling to the right edge clear of intersections until they pass, clearing a path when traffic bars pulling over, and still reaching the right shoulder even from the left lane under an officer stop, while lightless sirenless emergency vehicles earn no yield and every roadside vehicle including hazard-flashers deserves a leftward move or a slowdown [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec05-F09 | anchor: A02
At four-way stops and unsigned unsignaled crossings the first vehicle in owns the right-of-way, and simultaneous arrivals make the left driver yield to the right [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec05-F10 | anchor: A03
Intersections injure most, so slow early, scan both ways plus left again, roll in slow then accelerate clear, never brake mid-turn or mid-crossing, creep blind views to a stoppable pace, and refuse to enter blocked crossings until traffic ahead moves [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec05-F11 | anchor: A03
Flashing red bus lights or a red stop paddle mean boarding children and order a held stop until the bus rolls, the driver waves you on, or lights die with the sign folded, excused only across a different roadway, at controlled-access loading zones barring foot crossing, or as approaching traffic on a divided highway, and ignoring school-bus reds costs a mandatory one-year license revocation [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec05-F12 | anchor: A03
The Move Over or Bernardo-Mills Law under Title forty-seven section eleven-three hundred fourteen orders shifting a lane from stationary flashing-light roadside vehicles when safe or slowing with care, with multi-lane drivers leaving a buffer lane and two-lane drivers simply slowing, all to prevent distraction-fed secondary crashes [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec05-F13 | anchor: A04
A Traffic Incident Management scene is the roadway zone where responders work a crash, and move-over laws shield them by ordering lane changes away where possible or cautious slowing, with drivers staying alert, moving over, slowing down, obeying responder directions, and never rubbernecking past advance-warning, transition, and activity areas [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0031]
